Checks root, Xposed, adb, Shizuku, Termux and the module registry one by one; the result is copyable for a bug report.
su is a passthrough shell: every process already runs with root ids via the engine shim, and su provides the standard command-line behaviour (su, su -c, su -mm). Shizuku\'s root mode relies on it.

1. Put the module APK into the Download folder of internal storage (from the host: this system's shared storage-card folder).
2. Open the Install page, tap "Scan Download", then "Install" on the target APK.
3. On the Modules page tap "Enable".
4. Tap "Stop scope apps to apply", then reopen the target app.

Modules without a declared scope: check the framework state on the Diagnostics page, then reboot and retry.
Xposed/LSPosed modules ship on their repos\' GitHub Releases (CorePatch, QAuxiliary and friends are preinstalled). Pick the arm64 APK matching this system and drop it into Download.

AEmulator currently ships the Xposed API 101 declaration layer: modules install, enable and declare scopes normally, and the API classes and version are visible to them; but this build does not bundle an ART hook engine, so a module\'s actual hook calls do not take effect and its UI may say "not activated". That is the honest state of this build, not a malfunction. The Diagnostics page shows what works.
root comes from the AEmulator engine shim, not MagiskSU, so the Magisk app would report "Not installed". For root, modules and grants, use this manager.

Shizuku: when "start via wireless debugging" is not an option, root mode starts with one tap (the su chain is visible under Diagnostics).\nadb: ROM v4 preinstalls the adb client at /system/bin; the terminal (Termux) and this manager\'s install commands do not depend on the host.
Why preinstalled modules can only be disabled

Preinstalled modules live on the read-only /system partition; the guest cannot delete their files. "Disable" (pm disable) takes real effect: the app stops, its icon leaves the launcher, and it no longer loads inside its scope. To remove them completely, switch firmware images on the host side.
